claim_ceiling: Language-dominated baseline embeddings do not support legally coherent fractal mapping. Two independent methods improve the legal/language purity ratio by ~20% but no method achieves ratio >1.0. The resolution-dependent representation selector (baseline at domain, center-projected at subdomain, concat at microcluster) does NOT outperform using concat at all zoom levels. Concat achieves higher average legal purity (0.389 vs 0.347) and higher average ratio (0.418 vs 0.403).
evidence_summary: Independent audit of resolution-dependent representation selector experiment (run 33026205087, repair round=0). All 6 material quantitative claims independently recomputed from stored results: baseline avg legal purity 0.348546, baseline avg ratio 0.355439, concat avg legal purity 0.389168, concat avg ratio 0.417605, resolution-dependent avg legal purity 0.347125, resolution-dependent avg ratio 0.403045 — all match to 6 decimal places. All ratio calculations (legal_purity / lang_purity) verified correct. Per-resolution comparisons confirmed: concat beats baseline at every resolution (res 0.5: +18.8%, res 1.0: +2.0%, res 2.0: +20.3%, res 3.0: +8.0%). Cross-language similarity verified: baseline 0.869 vs concat 0.046. All 5 artifacts present and well-formed. No scope violations (no .opencode or .github files modified). No leakage, benchmark gaming, prettiness-as-quality bias, or unsupported product claims. Negative result honestly represented: hypothesis falsified, concat recommended at all zoom levels for intra-language legal navigation. One minor documentation inconsistency: docstring says 857 decisions, JSON says 1000 (857 is TF-IDF count, 1000 is full evaluation count). The recurring .opencode/agents/* scope violation pathology does not recur in this cycle.
